_readme: Claims this repo asserted, then RETRACTED at source. scripts/lint_retracted_claims.py fails
when one reappears in a markdown file without a retraction directive near it.
WHY A REGISTRY: a retraction is not self-enforcing. The claim below was corrected in three
PRs across two days and kept coming back, because correcting a surface does not stop the
next session from reading a dated record and re-deriving the claim into a live one -- which
is exactly how it reached the live WR2 orchestrator.
WHAT THIS LINT DOES NOT DO: it does not ban the tokens. Quoting a retracted claim in order
to correct it is the CURE. A hit is clean when a retraction DIRECTIVE sits within
`window_lines` of it. Deleting history is never the goal; a naked assertion is the target.
DIRECTIVES ARE CASE-SENSITIVE AND ALL-CAPS, ON PURPOSE. The first draft of this file used
ordinary words as markers -- including `Independent`, which is the very word the endorsement
it was supposed to catch contains ('Independent (no coordination) | 17.2x | MAI'). The guard
was absolved by the text it existed to catch: superscar #3 in its purest form, built during
a session about superscar #3. Ordinary words, adjectives and numbers are BANNED as
directives; `CORRECTED` is banned too because it is a substring of `uncorrected`.
CLAIM-BOUND ABSOLUTION (`absolution_pattern`). A directive proves that SOMETHING near this
line was retracted; it never says WHICH claim. With two claims registered, an annotation
about one would absolve a naked assertion of the other -- the gap this file pinned as
known_gap on day one. A claim carrying `absolution_pattern` now also requires a token from
its OWN correction in the window (for these two: the paper's real Table 5 numbers). A claim
WITHOUT one keeps the old any-directive behaviour: a declared limit, not an oversight.
TWO WAYS TO ABSOLVE, and the strong one is explicit. `RETRACTED[<claim-id>]` names the claim it
retracts and needs nothing else. The unstructured fallback (an ALL-CAPS directive PLUS this
claim's `absolution_pattern`) is NOT available to the two registered claims: both set
registry now REFUSES weak absolution tokens: a phrase that can occur inside the endorsement
(`no coordination`, `synthesis_only`, an architecture name) would absolve the very text it binds.
Directives are also negation-guarded: `NOT RETRACTED` contains `RETRACTED` and means its opposite.
DELIBERATE, DECLARED FRICTION: the lint flags ANY topical mention of a retracted claim, including
an accurate neutral one, and asks for a directive. A scanner cannot tell 'quoting the ratio
descriptively' from 'appealing to it', and this claim's entire history is one reader quoting it
neutrally and the next one re-deriving it as a reason. The cost is one directive per mention; the
alternative -- requiring a causal connective -- under-matches every bare appeal to 'the 17.2x
finding'. Pinned by test_declared_friction_accurate_neutral_mention_still_wants_a_directive.
MARKER-ONLY FOR REGISTERED CLAIMS (`require_bound_marker: true`, round 4). The unstructured
fallback is unsound and cannot be patched: the directive and the correction token are both
matched anywhere in the same window, so a naked endorsement can supply BOTH from its own words
(`Centralized > Independent confirms the rule; Table 5 reports Decentralized 0.477` sitting under
someone else's `RETRACTED`). Claim-specific correction evidence differs per claim anyway --
Table 4 STATISTICS for the causal claim, Table 5 VALUES for the ranking claim -- which is why the
readme's earlier 'both use the paper's real Table 5 numbers' was wrong. Only `RETRACTED[<id>]`
absolves a registered claim. The fallback remains for claims that do not opt in.

claims.source: arXiv:2512.08296v3 (Kim et al., Towards a Science of Scaling Agent Systems)
claims.what_was_claimed: that Google's 17.2x error-amplification finding is WHY subagents must never talk peer-to-peer
why_retracted: WRONG TOPOLOGY: 17.2x measures `Independent` -- S3.1 defines it as parallel agents with Omega=synthesis_only, i.e. NO coordination. Peer-to-peer is `Decentralized` (C={(ai,aj) for all i!=j}, debate rounds, consensus). The number never bore on the rule it was cited for.

UNSUPPORTED AS A CAUSE: S4.3 narrates error propagation as the mechanism, but Table 4 reports beta=0.014 CI[-0.047,0.074] p=0.658 and interaction beta=0.022 CI[-0.023,0.067] p=0.332; S4.3 concludes the gap is better explained by 'efficiency (Ec) and overhead (O%), rather than error propagation per se'.
PRECISION: p=0.658 means UNSUPPORTED, not disproved. The CIs straddle zero.

AND THE REPLACEMENT WAS WRONG TOO (found by cross-family review 2026-08-02, third generation of the same error): PRs #3513/#3514 replaced the causal claim with 'Independent worst, Centralized best'. Table 5 Success Rate says otherwise -- Decentralized 0.477, SAS 0.466, Centralized 0.463, Hybrid 0.452, Independent 0.370. Independent IS lowest, but Centralized is THIRD, below plain single-agent, and the paper states 'no single architecture dominates across all domains and vendors'. Worse for the rule this was cited for: `Decentralized` IS peer-to-peer and scores HIGHEST on that metric.
claims.what_still_stands: The no-peer-to-peer rule, unchanged -- but it rests on REPO GROUNDS ALONE (context isolation, one auditable state owner, no cross-worker contamination). This paper supports nothing about it in either direction, and on aggregate Success Rate its peer-to-peer architecture scores highest. Do not cite it for this rule at all.
claims.known_gap: CLOSED 2026-08-02 for the two registered claims by `absolution_pattern` (a directive must be accompanied by a token from this claim's own correction). Still open in general: a claim registered WITHOUT an absolution_pattern is absolved by any nearby directive. Pinned by test_known_gap_claim_without_absolution_is_not_bound.

claims.source: arXiv:2512.08296v3 (Kim et al.), Table 5 Success Rate
claims.what_was_claimed: that after withdrawing the 17.2x citation, the paper still SUPPORTS our no-peer-to-peer rule via its benchmark ranking -- phrased as 'Centralized best, Independent worst' or, in the weakened second draft, 'plus the paper's benchmark ranking (Centralized > Independent)'.
why_retracted: CENTRALIZED IS NOT BEST. Table 5 Success Rate: Decentralized 0.477 > SAS 0.466 > Centralized 0.463 > Hybrid 0.452 > Independent 0.370. Centralized is THIRD, below plain single-agent, and the paper states 'no single architecture dominates across all domains and vendors'.

THE PAIR IS TRUE AND IRRELEVANT. Centralized > Independent (0.463 > 0.370) does hold. It supports nothing about peers, because Independent is not peer-to-peer -- it is parallel agents with Omega=synthesis_only. Citing it as residual support is a non-sequitur.
IT POINTS THE WRONG WAY IF ANYTHING. The paper's peer-to-peer architecture is Decentralized, which scores HIGHEST on that metric.

THIRD GENERATION, SELF-INFLICTED. This claim was introduced by the sessions CORRECTING the 17.2x claim (#3513/#3514) and shipped to main. The lesson is not about one paper: a replacement assertion written while retracting another is unverified by default.

PATTERN LESSON (added after the cross-family round that caught this claim): the first regex matched only 'Centralized best' -- the exact wording I had written. It missed 'Centralized > Independent confirms the no-peer rule' and 'Independent is lowest, therefore use centralized state', which assert the same non-sequitur with no superlative in sight. A pattern written from the instance you found is a pattern that catches the instance you found.
claims.what_still_stands: The no-peer-to-peer rule, unchanged, on REPO GROUNDS ALONE (context isolation, one auditable state owner, no cross-worker contamination). Do not cite this paper for it in either direction.

claims.source: measured on M5 2026-08-08: readlink + stat -L + git rev-parse --absolute-git-dir
claims.what_was_claimed: that ~/Desktop/nuzantara is a real, separate checkout with a different inode from ~/nuzantara
why_retracted: IT IS A SYMLINK. `ls -ld` gives `lrwxr-xr-x ... -> /Users/balizero/nuzantara`; `stat -L` gives inode 758478 for BOTH paths; `git rev-parse --absolute-git-dir` answers /Users/balizero/nuzantara/.git for both. One checkout, two names.

HOW THE WRONG READING IS PRODUCED, which is why it will recur: `stat` WITHOUT -L reports the LINK's own inode (166687231). Comparing that against a directory's inode manufactures a difference that does not exist. Typing `stat` without -L is the natural thing to do, so this is a mistake to catch, not one to assume nobody repeats.

THE CONSEQUENCE RAN THE OPPOSITE WAY from what the claim implied. It was written to describe a cron writing to a harmless side copy; the truth is that `com.balizero.nuzantara-repo-sync` was aimed at the MAIN checkout, under live sibling work, and would have `git merge --ff-only`d on top of it the moment its tracked edits cleared. A future reader who re-derives 'separate checkout' will under-rate exactly that class of risk.
claims.what_still_stands: The daemon's disposition (retired, Option A, 2026-08-08) and every OTHER measurement in the ledger line and the decision record. Only the identity of ~/Desktop/nuzantara was wrong.
